page: Amazon Web Services c8i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 64-vCPU allocation across 32 physical cores using the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. The processor includes 480 MB of shared L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is 128.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. The instance has no local bundled storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance and instruction execution speed. The instance achieved top-tier rankings in Geekbench multi-core with a score of 21074.0, Clang software compilation at 59767.0, and static web serving throughput reaching 107.02 GB/sec. Parallelized integer and floating-point computations show similar strength, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 82984.7 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 69204.24. Thanks to DDR5 bandwidth reaching up to 197.26 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads, the platform also delivers strong throughput for memory-bound tasks, registering 114.83 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the compute-heavy design and local storage profile. With a 2 GB per vCPU ratio and zero local NVMe storage, memory-dense databases or workloads that require high-throughput temporary scratch disks will need specialized instance families or external storage provisioning. However, for compute-intensive automation, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving at scale, and CPU-driven AMX-accelerated matrix operations, the instance offers significant computational resource density.
The Amazon Web Services c8i.16xlarge is suited for software build farms, parallel distributed computing, media encoding, high-traffic static web servers, and batch data processing.
